briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East conflict has escalated drastically in the past 24 hours, marking the seventh consecutive night of extensive US strikes targeting critical Iranian civilian and military infrastructure across southern Iran, resulting in multiple casualties and widespread damage. Concurrently, Iran has launched retaliatory ballistic missile and drone attacks against US bases and assets in Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Iraq, while explicitly threatening a "full-scale offensive" and closure of the Strait of Hormuz if US aggression continues. The US is deploying dozens of additional refueling aircraft to Israel, signaling preparations for a potentially much broader military operation.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran intensified, marking the seventh consecutive night of US strikes. CENTCOM reported striking dozens of Iranian military targets including coastal observation and air defense facilities, military logistical infrastructure, and naval capabilities. Five bridges in southern Iran were reported hit by the US Army, affecting routes to Bandar Abbas and Sirjan, including Shahid Mirzaei Tunnel, Shour River Bridge, and the Minab-Roodan axis bridge. The S. Kalantari Port observation tower in Chabahar, used by the IRGC for surveillance of the Strait of Hormuz, was also destroyed. An empty oil tanker, Belma NI 22, was reportedly hit by two US missiles near Kharg Island. Attacks were reported in Ahvaz (Khuzestan), Yazd (central Iran, 5 missiles outside city), Sirik (Hormozgan, 3-4 explosions), Lar, Darab (Fars province), Qeshm Island, and Bushehr. An MQ9 drone was reportedly shot down over Bushehr by IRGC Navy air defense, and an RQ-11 drone was also downed in southern Iran.

Iranian retaliatory operations included drone attacks on US ammunition depots and headquarters at Al-Udeiri and Ali Al-Salem bases in Kuwait, as well as fuel tanks at the Al-Azraq base in Jordan. Iran also claimed to have destroyed the main AI center and an unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) depot in Bahrain using ballistic missiles and drones. Ballistic missiles were launched at a US base in Saudi Arabia, specifically targeting Al-Kharj and Yanbu. The IRGC Navy claimed to have stopped four "illegal" vessels in the Strait of Hormuz with US backing, and separately attacked a Thai-flagged vessel for ignoring warnings and attempting to cross without IRGC permission. The IRGC also claimed two oil tankers exploded and caught fire in a mined area south of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Army reported firing cruise missiles at a hostile vessel in the northern Indian Ocean, forcing it to flee.

The human cost in Iran has been significant, with the Ministry of Health reporting at least 38 killed and over 400 injured since the renewed fighting with the US. Hormozgan province alone reported 8 martyrs and 8 injured from recent US attacks, including two disabled brothers and three women killed on a bridge. Civilian infrastructure damage has prompted the Hormozgan governorate to warn residents against unnecessary travel and close roads. Reports of fuel shortages in Zahedan and water/electricity cuts in Tehran and Karaj suggest internal strain.

Leadership decisions and statements include Mohsen Rezaei, advisor to the leader, threatening a "full-scale offensive and complete destruction of the enemy" if US attacks continue for another 2-3 days, stating no political boundary would be safe and the "negotiation and war" policy has ended. The IRGC Navy Commander Ali Ozmaei vowed to "turn the sea into hell for the Americans." IRGC Aerospace Force Commander Brigadier General Majid Mousavi stated strikes would continue until calm is restored to Iran's southern coastline and the Strait of Hormuz. The Supreme National Security Council has reportedly directed media to avoid publishing details on damage to civilian infrastructure or service disruptions, citing "wartime conditions." A confidential report to the Iranian presidency suggests only 9% of Iranians support the status quo, with nearly three-quarters favoring deep reform or outright replacement of the political system. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei accused the US of showing weakness by killing innocents and called on the UN to hold the US responsible for war crimes.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included an interceptor missile launch towards a "false identification" over the southern Gaza Strip, with no sirens activated and no security incident reported. A Hamas company commander, Anas Mahmoud Ahmad Hamdan, described as a "central figure in holding hostages" and "right-hand man" to Muhammad Deif and Rafa'a Salameh, was killed in an Israeli strike in Khan Younis, Gaza.

The home front experienced several internal security incidents, including violent events near the Dead Sea, Segev Shalom, and Haifa. In the southern Golan Heights, Israeli settlement activists illegally crossed the border into Syria on Thursday and were apprehended today, prompting the IDF to warn of increased attempts to cross into Syria, which divert military attention and compromise security. Another incident in Gush Etzion involved an Israeli citizen hitting a minor and dragging a woman, causing minor injuries. Military prosecution filed an indictment against Shadi Juma for the 2007 murder of Ido Zoldan.

Politically, the Knesset voted for its dissolution, paving the way for national elections likely on October 27th. The Attorney General advised ministers that the country is in an interim government period, requiring consultation before non-routine decisions. Legislation passed included the extension of mandatory military service to 32 months. Prime Minister Netanyahu issued a direct warning to Iran, stating, "Do not count on it being quiet if you attack us. This will be a different event, much more powerful."

GAZA & WEST BANK
A Hamas company commander, Anas Mahmoud Ahmad Hamdan, described as a "central figure in holding hostages" and involved in Hamas's propaganda in Khan Younis, was killed in an Israeli strike in the Gaza Strip. Additionally, an Israeli airstrike killed at least eight Palestinians and wounded over 20 others at a funeral in the central Gaza Strip. An Israeli drone strike west of the Nuseirat refugee camp killed one Palestinian and wounded several others. In the West Bank, five Palestinians were arrested near Ma'ale Tidar in the southern Hebron Hills for allegedly attacking Israeli shepherds with stones, causing minor head injuries. An incident in Gush Etzion involved an Israeli citizen hitting a minor and dragging a woman, causing light injuries.

LEBANON
Israeli fighter jets were reported to be flying over Beirut. A security incident occurred in south Lebanon, with Israeli helicopters reportedly evacuating several individuals to Rambam hospital. Anti-regime social media posts celebrated the destruction of a mosque in south Lebanon, framing it as a "blessing of the resistance."

SYRIA & IRAQ
Iran launched drone attacks against US forces and assets in the region. The Iranian Army reported targeting fuel tanks at the Al-Azraq base in Jordan and ammunition depots and headquarters at Al-Udeiri base in Kuwait. Multiple sources confirmed Iranian missile strikes on the US Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, with CBS reporting several US troops injured there. Satellite imagery analysis by Faytuks Network indicates damage to the US-Jordanian Prince Hassan Air Base, potentially affecting its ability to accommodate large aircraft. Jordan reported intercepting three Iranian missiles over its territory.

In Syria, the IRGC claimed to have attacked the Al-Tanf base, which previously hosted US forces, though US CENTCOM stated US forces had withdrawn in April and refuted claims of casualties or captures.

In Iraq, two drone attacks were reported at a camp of Kurdish-Iranian opposition forces in northern Iraq. Multiple drone attacks, with at least five suicide drones, targeted Erbil, activating Patriot air defense systems. Flights at Erbil airport were canceled due to attacks on the nearby US Harir base. Sulaymaniyah also experienced drone attacks on an anti-Iran separatist terrorist camp, with reports of a fire at an ammunition depot and drones still flying over the province. Iran's Army reported 11 cross-border operations by its Nohed 65th Brigade in Iraqi Kurdistan, eliminating 8 mid-level separatist commanders and destroying 3 headquarters. Diplomatic developments include the US State Department announcing Iraq-Syria cooperation on rehabilitating the Iraq-Syria crude oil pipeline.

GULF STATES
The Gulf states were heavily impacted by direct Iranian attacks and significant regional tensions.
*   **Kuwait:** The Kuwaiti Army reported facing an Iranian drone attack and detected hostile ballistic missiles and drones in its airspace. Iran's Army confirmed drone attacks on US ammunition depots at Al-Udeiri and headquarters/ammunition at Ali Al-Salem, as well as several bridges in Kuwait. Kuwait's state news agency reported that two fires at attacked sites in the south were brought under control, with no casualties. Kuwait's Ministry of Electricity, Water, and Renewable Energy stated that a power generation and desalination plant was hit, causing damage to multiple units and fires, but no casualties were reported by Kuwait. Kuwait International Airport temporarily ceased operations due to Iranian missile attacks.
*   **Bahrain:** Alarms were sounded across Bahrain, with reports of violent explosions. The IRGC claimed to have destroyed a US unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) depot and the main AI center, used for enemy targeting, using ballistic missiles and drones. Aircraft reportedly fled Bahraini airspace following the Iranian missile attack. Iranian air attacks in Bahrain were reportedly intercepted.
*   **Qatar:** The IRGC claimed to have attacked the US Al-Udeid base. Satellite imagery analysis indicated damage to facilities at Al-Udeid. Explosions were also reported in Doha. Qatar's Ministry of Defense announced it had foiled an air attack, and its Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned Iran's attack on Iraqi Kurdistan, calling it a violation of Iraqi sovereignty.
*   **Saudi Arabia:** A US official reported that Iran launched a ballistic missile at a US base in Saudi Arabia, marking the first direct Iranian attack on the Kingdom in nearly four months. Sirens sounded in cities like Al-Kharj and Yanbu after missile launches from Iran, with reports of US military bases being targeted.
*   **Strait of Hormuz:** The IRGC declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely closed" and "severely unsafe" due to "US child-killing army's crimes," vowing no oil or gas exports until US aggression ends. They claimed two oil tankers exploded and caught fire in a "mined area" south of the Strait, citing "US intelligence deception." The IRGC Navy also reported stopping four "illegal" vessels and targeting a Thai-flagged vessel that allegedly ignored warnings. Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz hit a three-week low, with nearly all vessels using IRGC-approved routes. The International Energy Agency warned that global energy security is at risk due to the disruption. Houthi-Saudi hostilities threaten a crucial oil-export pipeline route Saudi Arabia uses to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

Pakistan expressed deep concern over renewed Houthi-Saudi fighting, fearing being drawn into the war, and stated that attacks on Saudi Arabia are considered attacks on Pakistan. Pakistan is reportedly negotiating an expanded defense pact with Kuwait in exchange for energy cooperation. The UAE has not issued any statements regarding the disputed three islands, a change noted by some sources.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Launches Seventh Consecutive Night of Strikes on Iran:** CENTCOM conducted a new wave of extensive attacks across southern Iran, targeting military and civilian infrastructure including bridges, port facilities, air defense systems, and potentially energy sites.
2.  **Iran Retaliates with Direct Attacks on US Bases and Gulf States:** Iran launched ballistic missiles and drones against US military bases in Saudi Arabia (Al-Kharj, Yanbu), Jordan (Muwaffaq Salti, Al-Azraq, Prince Hassan bases, causing US casualties), Kuwait (Al-Udeiri, Ali Al-Salem bases, bridges, power/desalination plant), and claimed destruction of US assets in Bahrain (AI center, UUV depot).
3.  **Iran Threatens "Full-Scale Offensive" and Hormuz Closure:** Mohsen Rezaei, advisor to Iran's leader, warned of a "full-scale offensive and complete destruction of the enemy" if US attacks continue for 2-3 days, stating no political boundaries would be safe. The IRGC declared the Strait of Hormuz "completely closed" to oil/gas exports, stating it is "severely unsafe."
4.  **US Deploys Dozens of Refueling Aircraft to Israel:** The Trump administration informed Israel of its intention to send dozens of additional refueling planes to Israel in preparation for a possible expanded military operation against Iran. Over 60 US refueling aircraft have reportedly arrived in Israel, with 33 at Ben Gurion Airport.
5.  **First Direct Iranian Ballistic Missile Attack on Saudi Arabia in Four Months:** Iran launched a ballistic missile at a US base in Saudi Arabia, marking the first such direct attack in nearly four months.
6.  **Significant Iranian Casualties and Infrastructure Damage:** Iran's Health Ministry reported at least 38 killed and over 400 injured since renewed US fighting. Hormozgan province specifically reported 8 martyrs, including civilians, from US attacks on bridges and other infrastructure.
7.  **Iranian Rial Crashes to Historic Low:** The Iranian Rial continued its decline, reaching 1,918,000 to one US dollar, reflecting severe economic pressure.
8.  **Hamas Company Commander Killed in Gaza:** Anas Mahmoud Ahmad Hamdan, a company commander in Hamas described as a "central figure in holding hostages" and a "right-hand man" to Muhammad Deif, was killed in an Israeli strike in Khan Younis.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
**Escalation Risks:** The risk of severe escalation is critical. Iran's explicit threat of a "full-scale offensive" that transcends political boundaries, coupled with its warning to target US-linked industrial, IT, and AI assets across the region if its infrastructure is attacked, indicates a willingness to broaden the conflict significantly. The deployment of US refueling aircraft to Israel and consideration of strikes on Iranian power plants and nuclear facilities by the Trump administration suggest preparations for a broader offensive beyond current strikes. Hebrew media speculates about a potential "ground attack from the south" involving NATO, Kurdish, Israeli, and Arab forces.
**Active Flashpoints:** The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with Iran's declaration of its closure and reports of mined areas. Direct attacks on US bases across Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan, along with continuous strikes on Iranian southern provinces, indicate widespread and active combat zones. Iraqi Kurdistan (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah) is experiencing intensified proxy/drone attacks. The potential for a direct Israeli-Iranian confrontation is high, especially if US operations are launched from Israeli soil. Renewed Houthi-Saudi hostilities also threaten regional oil bypass routes.
**Military Posture Changes:** The deployment of dozens of US refueling aircraft to Israel, including specialized F-16CJ fighter jets to Jordan, signifies an enhanced US offensive posture, preparing for potential deeper strikes into Iran. CENTCOM has also increased its alert level across US bases in the region. Iran's Navy warnings about US naval units nearing "zero hour" suggest its forces are on high alert.
**Red Lines:** Iran has drawn a clear red line regarding further US attacks on its infrastructure, threatening destruction of US-linked industrial and technological assets in any host country. Pakistan has issued a stern warning to Iran, stating that attacks on Saudi Arabia are considered attacks on Pakistan, highlighting its own potential entry into the conflict if the Houthi-Saudi situation deteriorates further.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** CENTCOM confirmed the seventh consecutive night of strikes against Iran, aiming to weaken its military capabilities and hold it accountable for commercial shipping attacks. The US is reportedly sending dozens of additional refueling planes to Israel, with over 60 already having arrived, in preparation for a potential expansion of military operations. US officials are considering options including striking Iranian power plants, further attacks on nuclear facilities (e.g., Pickaxe Mountain). CENTCOM also increased its alert level at all US bases in the region due to potential attacks. The US Embassy reissued a travel warning for Israel and advised staff to reconsider travel to the Middle East. US State Department announced Iraq-Syria cooperation on rehabilitating the Iraq-Syria crude oil pipeline.
**Gulf States:** Kuwait's military and critical infrastructure have been directly targeted by Iran, leading to fires and temporary airport closures. Bahrain experienced widespread alarms and confirmed Iranian strikes on its AI center and UUV depot. Qatar's Ministry of Defense foiled an air attack and officially condemned Iran's attack on Iraqi Kurdistan, violating Iraqi sovereignty. Saudi Arabia also saw US bases targeted by Iranian ballistic missiles. Pakistan, a key regional ally, expressed serious concern about the Houthi-Saudi conflict and is reportedly negotiating an expanded defense pact with Kuwait in exchange for energy cooperation. Yemenis held rallies supporting Iran and denouncing Saudi aggression.
**United Kingdom:** The UK officially designated the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) as an illegal group based on the 2026 National Security (State Threats) Act. UK police charged a 39-year-old man from Liverpool for aiding Iranian intelligence. A SkyNews investigation, based on expert analysis, concluded the US was responsible for an attack on the Shajarat Tayebah school in Minab, killing children.
**Jordan:** Jordanian authorities confirmed intercepting three Iranian missiles, reporting no casualties or damage. However, US CBS News reported several US troops were injured from Iranian strikes on two bases in Jordan.
**International Organizations:** The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that global energy security is at risk due to oil shipment disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran sent a letter to the UN Security Council, accusing the US of war crimes and demanding full international responsibility for loss of life, injuries, and infrastructure destruction.
**Colombia:** The newly appointed leader of Colombia, Abelardo de la Aspriella, announced the withdrawal of Colombia's lawsuit against Israel at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), signaling a renewal of diplomatic ties.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
1.  **Contradictory Claims on Hormuz Tanker Attacks:** CENTCOM directly refuted the IRGC's claim that two oil tankers exploded after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, calling the claim "untrue."
2.  **N12 Misreport on Iranian Vessel Attack:** N12 initially reported "Iran Army: we attacked an Iranian vessel in the Indian Ocean." This contradicts other sources, including Iran's Army (via Press TV and Shargh Daily), which stated they attacked an *enemy* vessel. This appears to be a mistranslation or miscommunication by N12.
3.  **Disputed Al-Tanf Base Attack:** The IRGC claimed to have attacked the US Al-Tanf base in eastern Syria. However, CENTCOM explicitly refuted this, stating that the last US forces withdrew from Syria in April and no US personnel were killed or captured.
4.  **Conflicting Reports on US Refueling Plane Numbers in Israel:** N12 reported that the US had not transferred additional refueling planes and planned to reduce numbers to about 20. This directly contradicted other N12 reports, as well as those from Axios and Faytuks Network, which stated the Trump administration was sending "dozens more" refueling planes to Israel, with over 60 already present. This discrepancy could indicate internal debate or conflicting information flows within US/Israeli circles.
5.  **Patriot System Performance in Jordan:** Iranian sources (NAYA) and affiliated media claimed that Iranian missiles struck US bases in Jordan with "total failure" of the Patriot missile defense system to intercept. However, N12 reported that Jordan had successfully intercepted three Iranian missiles, without specifying if these were the same ones targeting US bases. A Jordanian source to NAYA also claimed no interceptions and direct hits, contradicting other reports.
6.  **Conflicting Reports on Strikes in Iranian Cities:** There are numerous contradictions regarding specific US strike locations and their impact. Local sources reported explosions in Lar, Bushehr, and Bandar Abbas, but officials (Fars Governor, Hormozgan Governor, Bushehr Governor) later denied hits or reported them as outside city limits, suggesting either confusion, rapid changes in assessment, or attempts to downplay damage. Similarly, initial reports of explosions in Ahvaz were later unconfirmed by Mehr News.
7.  **Iranian Media Control and Propaganda:** Iran's Supreme National Security Council reportedly issued a directive to media outlets to avoid publishing details on damage to civilian infrastructure, the scale of destruction, or disruptions to public services. This directive aimed to prevent public fear and obscure the extent of the enemy's success, suggesting a deliberate effort to manage public perception and control information during the conflict.
8.  **Bushehr Nuclear Plant Status:** Press TV ran an "Exclusive" report denying that any US strike hit the Bushehr nuclear power plant, specifically rejecting an Al Jazeera report. This is a crucial clarification, but could also serve as a propaganda point to assure the public about the safety of sensitive facilities.
